scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5012: Office A users (e.g. PC1, 10.1.0.100) report that
since this morning they have completely lost Internet access -- web pages
time out and nothing outside the office loads. The team suspects the R1
Internet uplink or the ISP went down overnight. Please find and confirm the
fault, and tell us which device or link to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  Office A reaches the Internet via R1's NAT. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the egress path --
  does the agent verify Internet reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate an uplink/ISP fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office A has lost
all Internet access -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaches the ISP
edge 203.0.113.1 with 0% loss, because R1
MASQUERADEs 10.1.0.0/24 out its ISP uplinks (eth2/eth3) and its default route
and OSPF adjacencies to CSW1/CSW2 are intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the egress path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the Office A -> Internet path against the live lab (ping/curl a public
address, check R1's NAT and default route), finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming the R1 uplink, an ISP, or
NAT to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead
of testing it.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the lab is an isolated emulation --
"the Internet" is the emulated ISP edge (203.0.113.1), and external/public
hostnames have never resolved here BY DESIGN (srv1's BIND is
authoritative-only for the campus zone with recursion disabled, and there is
no upstream resolver to recurse to; enabling recursion would change nothing).
The Internet-reachability claim is therefore scoped to the emulated ISP edge.
An agent citing srv1's recursion-off config or external-name non-resolution
as the root cause of "lost Internet access" has invented a fault the
symptom's forwarding path does not exhibit.

agent.diagnosis_text: The network is completely healthy. All components that the ticket hypothesises as faulty were directly verified to be operational. R1's two WAN uplinks are both up and holding valid DHCP addresses from their respective ISPs: eth2 (203.0.113.2/30, facing ISPA) and eth3 (203.0.113.6/30, facing ISPB). R1 has an active kernel default route via 203.0.113.1 (ISPA) and is redistributing it into OSPF via `default-information originate`. All interior routers — csw1, csw2, dswa1, dswa2, dswb1, dswb2 — are receiving the OSPF-originated default route with ECMP paths through both core switches. NAT masquerade rules for every internal subnet (10.1–10.6.0.0/24) are installed on R1 and were observed actively processing packets (17 hits / 1044 bytes on the 10.1.0.0/24 → eth2 rule after a single ping session from PC1). End-to-end Internet reachability was confirmed from three different Office A devices: PC1 (10.1.0.100) reached 172.253.62.100, 66.235.200.145 (ISPA loopbacks), and 216.239.35.4 (ISPB loopback) with 0% packet loss; pc2 and laptop1 both reached the ISPA gateway (203.0.113.1) without loss. The ISP RFC1918 ingress filters on ISPA and ISPB are correctly configured security policy and do not affect post-NAT Internet traffic. The root cause of the ticket is a false premise — there is no Internet outage; the R1 uplinks and ISP peers are fully operational and Office A users have uninterrupted Internet connectivity. No corrective action is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes R1's NAT rules, default route, and OSPF adjacencies are intact at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly verifies R1's NAT masquerade rules, an active/default route via 203.0.113.1, and OSPF default-route distribution/receipt (implying adjacencies are intact).

The agent ran appropriate checks (host routes, R1 config/routes, OSPF, NAT counters, and multiple end-to-end pings) and the log shows successful reachability and NAT activity, so the conclusion of no outage is well supported.
